q: If I use Tatsugiri ex's "Cinnabar Lure" attack, can I choose to put Stage 1 or Stage 2 Pokemon cards directly onto my Bench?
a: Yes, as long as there is room on your Bench to put them.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If my opponent put a Stage 1 Pokemon directly into play using Tatsugiri ex's "Cinnabar Lure" attack, and I use Paldean Tauros' "Spirited Tackle" attack while that Pokemon is Active, would it do 90 or 180 damage?
a: It does 180 damage. Although the Stage 1 Pokemon is not an "Evolved Pokemon" in this scenario, it is still considered an "Evolution Pokemon" (Stage 1) that meets the requirements for Spirited Tackle.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: In Prereleases where we start the game with 4 Prize Cards each, how much damage does Gouging Fire's "Blazing Charge" attack do?
a: Blazing Charge would do 170 damage (100+70) since each player starts the game with 4 Prize Cards.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I use Armarouge's "Crimson Blaster" attack but my opponent has no benched Pokemon, do I still discard all my {R} energy?
a: Yes, but it would not do any damage to the Active Pokemon.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I use Rotom's "Crushing Pulse" attack, may I choose to not discard certain Item or Tool cards from my opponent's hand?
a: No, you must discard all of them.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If my opponent has no benched Pokemon, do I do 40 damage to their Active Pokemon when I use Braviary's "Drag Off" attack?
a: No. Damage is only done to the "new Active Pokemon". If there is no switch, then no damage is done.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I Knock Out my opponent's Active Pokemon with Wo-Chien's "Entangling Whip" attack and take my last prize card but also discard the last cards in my deck, do I win or lose because I have no cards left in my deck?
a: You win. You lose if you can't draw a card at the start of your turn, but since you took your last prize the game ends before that happens.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: Can I use Vivillon's "Evo-Powder" attack to evolve Basic Pokemon that I just put into play this turn?
a: Yes, you can.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I use Walrein's "Frigid Fangs" attack and on my opponent's turn they somehow move Walrein to the Bench, do they still need more than 2 Energy attached to their Pokemon to attack?
a: Yes. The effect resides on all of the opponent's Pokemon, not on Walrein, so moving Walrein to the Bench does not get rid of the effect.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

topics: Attacks » Now You're in My Power
q: Does Oranguru's "Now You're in My Power" attack mean the Defending Pokemon is now weak to all types?
a: No, not all types. It only makes it weak to Colorless Type Pokemon.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

topics: Attacks » Now You're in My Power
q: If a Pokemon has no Weakness to begin with, does Oranguru's "Now You're in My Power" attack give it a Weakness to {C}?
a: Yes. If a Pokemon has no Weakness printed on the card, Oranguru's attack will give that Pokemon a x2 Weakness of Colorless.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I use Stunfisk's "Paralyzing Crackle" attack and flip tails, do I still get to discard an Energy card from my Opponent's Active Pokemon?
a: No, the coin flip is for both Paralyzing the Pokemon and discarding the Energy card.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: Terapagos' "Prism Charge" attack can attach energy to "Tera Pokemon", but can I attach that energy to this Terapagos?
a: No, although Terapagos' *category* is literally "Tera Pokemon" that doesn't count for the purposes of this attack which only counts for Pokemon with the "Tera Pokemon" attribute.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I use Koraidon's "Unrelenting Onslaught" attack, can I get the extra bonus damage if I attacked last turn with a different Koraidon?
a: Yes. Unrelenting Onslaught only cares about whether a different Ancient Pokemon attacked during your last turn.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I have only 1 card left in my deck and my Pokemon with the Amulet of Hope tool attached is KO'd do I have to take that card and put it into my hand?
a: Yes. You must take at least 1 card with Amulet of Hope when it applies.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I play Brilliant Blender but don't want to discard any of the cards in my deck, can I choose to discard no cards?
a: No, you must discard at least one card from your deck if you play Brilliant Blender.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: For Energy Search Pro, can I search for multiple Basic Energy cards of different types, like 3 Grass and 2 Fire and 4 Water?
a: No, you can only put ONE card of each energy type into your hand.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: What happens if I play Megaton Blower and there's not a Stadium, a Tool, or a Special Energy in play?
a: You can't play the card for no effect, but if there is at least one of those types of cards in play you do as much as you can.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: Can I use Megaton Blower if there's a Stadium in play but my opponent doesn't have any Tools or Special Energy cards in play?
a: Yes, you can. Discarding the Stadium is not reliant upon discarding any other cards in this case.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: Can I use Surfer to switch my Active Pokemon with a benched Pokemon, even if I have no cards left in my deck?
a: Sure thing, bro!
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I have no Pokemon on my bench can I play Surfer?
a: No way, dude! You must be able to switch a Pokemon from the Bench in order to play Surfer.
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: If I play Tyme, can I put a Ceruledge ex face down and say "Ceruledge"?
a: No, you have to state the full card name. In this case, "Ceruledge ex".
source: Surging Sparks FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2024-11-07)

q: Does Gravity Gemstone add to the Retreat Cost of my Pokemon while I have Latias ex with "Skyliner" Ability or Archuladon with "Metal Bridge" Ability in play?
a: Nope, if a Pokemon is set to have no Retreat Cost by an effect such as Skyliner or Metal Bridge, it cannot be increased.

q: If I have 4 Togekiss with "Wonder Kiss" Ability in play when my opponent's Active Pokemon is Knocked Out, do I get to flip 4 times even though I can only take one extra prize, assuming one of the flips is heads?
a: No, you only get to flip once. "The effect of Wonder Kiss does not stack" means that you can only use the Ability once regardless of how many Togekiss are in play. The coin flip is part of using the Ability, so you can't "stack" the flips.

q: If Dusknoir or Dusclops is in the Active Spot and uses its "Cursed Blast" Ability to KO a Togekiss with "Wonder Kiss" Ability, does Togekiss get to take an extra Prize Card or not?
a: If the Dusknoir or Dusclops is active when they use Cursed Blast, Wonder Kiss will apply.

q: If I use Ceruledge's "Cursed Edge" attack while Temple of Sinnoh is in play, do I get to discard my opponent's attached Special Energy cards?
a: Yes. While their effects may be turned off, they are still considered Special Energy cards.

q: If I use Koraidon's "Unrelenting Onslaught" attack, can I get the extra bonus damage if my different Ancient Pokemon attacked while confused and flipped tails?
a: No. A failed attack attempt while Confused does not count as an attack.

q: Does the Errata for Lucky Egg from May 2010 apply to the newest version of Lucky Egg (SW:Sword & Shield, 167/202) even though the new version was released several years after the Errata and still contains the same text as the pre-Errata version of the card?
a: No, the newer version of the card should be played as written.

q: If Dusknoir is Active and uses its "Cursed Blast" Ability to KO a Togekiss with "Wonder Kiss" Ability, would Togekiss still get to flip for Dusknoir being KO'd or not?
a: Yes, you would get to flip for Wonder Kiss. All effects have to be resolved before resolving KO's.

q: At the end of my turn, both players' Active Pokemon are Poisoned. During Pokemon Checkup my opponent's poisoned Pokemon gets KO'd, and they bring up a Pecharunt with "Toxic Subjugation" Ability. Does my Active Pokemon then receive additional damage counters for poison placed on it?
a: Both Poisoned Pokemon receive damage counters during Pokemon Checkup, then you check to see if any Pokemon are Knocked Out. A new Active Pokemon is promoted after the check for Special Conditions. So when Pecharunt is promoted Pokemon Checkup is already over and Toxic Subjugation would not apply.

q: If I use Lumineon V's "Aqua Return" attack against a Defending Pokemon with a Handheld Fan attached, does the Handheld Fan move an Energy from Lumineon V to one of my Benched Pokemon or does the Energy get shuffled into the deck due to "Aqua Return"?
a: Aqua Return puts Lumineon V into the deck as part of its attack before the Energy can be moved for Handheld Fan's effect. The order of operations is that effects of the Pokemon's attack happen first, and then any triggered effects on the Defending Pokemon happen next.

q: If I have an Ancient Pokemon in the Active Spot that attacked last turn and I use Thorton to switch it for a Koraidon with "Unrelenting Onslaught" attack, would I get the bonus damage for "Unrelenting Onslaught"?
a: No, all effects carry over when using Thorton, so the game sees Koraidon as the same Pokemon for all intents and purposes, including having attacked last turn.

q: If Festival Grounds stadium is in play and my Dipplin with the "Festival Lead" Ability attacks and KO's my opponent's Active Flutter Mane with the "Midnight Fluttering" Ability, can Dipplin attack a second time?
a: Yes you can, because Festival Lead is no longer disabled after Flutter Mane is KO'd.

q: Say Mew ex used its "Genome Hacking" attack last turn to copy Sylveon ex's "Angelite" attack. If I use "Genome Hacking" this turn to copy the same attack, can I shuffle 2 of their Benched Pokemon into their deck again?
a: Yes, you can. Mew ex used "the effect" of Angelite last turn, but the "attack" it did was Genome Hacking, so the restriction of Angelite does not apply.

q: Does my active Sylveon's "Safeguard" Ability prevent Cornerstone Mask Ogerpon's "Demolish" attack?
a: No. Safeguard is an effect on Sylveon, and Demolish ignores effects on your opponent's Active Pokemon.

q: If I use Hop's Dubwool's "Defiant Horn" Ability, who chooses which Benched Pokemon is moved up?
a: The person using the Ability get to choose.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I attack Maractus that has the "Exploding Needles" Ability with a damaged Lillie's Comfey's "Fade Out" attack, would I put 6 damage counters on Lillie's Comfey and knock it out before it goes to the hand?
a: No, Lillie's Comfey would go to the hand first and then Exploding Needles would be triggered and find no valid target.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: Will Lillie's Clefairy ex's "Fairy Zone" Ability give a Weakness to {N} type Pokemon that don't currently have a Weakness?
a: Yes it will!
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: Can I use Iono's Kilowattrel's "Flashing Draw" Ability if I have no cards in my deck?
a: No. The effect of Flashing Draw is to draw cards, so if you have no cards in your deck or if you already have 6 or more cards in hand you can't use it.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: Can you use Lillie's Ribombee's "Inviting Wink" Ability if your opponent's Bench is full?
a: No. It's public knowledge that you can't put down any additional Basic Pokemon on your opponent's Bench, so you cannot use the Ability.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: When using Lillie's Ribombee's "Inviting Wink" Ability to put Pokemon onto my opponent's Bench, are they allowed to evolve those Pokemon on their next turn since they just came into play?
a: Yes, as long as it's not the opponent's first turn of the game they can evolve those Pokemon if they are able to do so. It is a basic game rule that neither player can normally evolve any Pokemon on their first turn of the game, even if they are going second.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I use Lillie's Ribombee's "Inviting Wink" Ability and my opponent has Basic Pokemon in their hand that I don't want to put in play, do I have to choose at least one Pokemon?
a: No, you can choose to put zero Pokemon onto the opponent's Bench.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I have Magmortar with the "Magma Surge" Ability, does it place 3 total damage counters for Burn between turns?
a: No, this is an additive effect, so during Pokemon Checkup each Burned Pokemon takes two damage counters for Burn and three more damage counters for Magmortar's "Magma Surge". For example, if there is a second Magmortar, Burn would do 2+3+3 for a total of 8 damage counters.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: How is Grimmsnarl's "Shadowy Knot" attack affected by Toedscruel's "Secret Forest Path" Ability?
a: Reduce the retreat cost by {C}{C}, then calculate the damage done by Shadowy Knot from the remaining retreat cost, if any.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)
Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: Can I use N's Zoroark ex's "Trade" Ability if there are no cards in my deck, just to discard a card?
a: No, you can't use Trade if there aren't any cards left in your deck. Discarding a card from your hand is a cost to use the Ability, and drawing cards is the effect.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I use Bombirdier's "Drop Shot" attack and accidentally choose an opponent's Benched Pokemon that can't be damaged (a Tera Pokemon, for example) do I still have to discard all Energy since I wouldn't do any damage?
a: Yes, even if you can't do any damage, you still discard the Energy.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I use N's Darmanitan "Flamebody Cannon" attack but my opponent has no benched Pokemon, do I still have to discard all energy from N's Darmanitan?
a: Flamebody Cannon requires you to discard all the Energy even if your opponent has no Benched Pokemon.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I use Volcanion ex's "Scorching Cyclone" attack and I have no Benched Pokemon does an Energy get discarded or not?
a: If you have no benched Pokemon no Energy is moved or discarded. The attack damage still happens.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I use Iono's Voltorb's "Voltaic Chain" attack and one of my Pokemon has a Luminous Energy attached, will it do an extra 20 damage for that?
a: Yes. The attack does not specify that it has to be Basic {L} Energy, so Luminous Energy will count while it is attached to one of Iono's Pokemon.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I play the Supporter Ruffian, can I choose a Tool on one Pokemon and a Special Energy from another?
a: No, they have to be from the same Pokemon.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If an Active Pokemon has 2 Spiky Energy attached and an opponent's attack damages them, does the Attacking Pokemon take 2 damage counters or 4?
a: 4 damage counters would be placed on the attacking Pokemon. The effect of Spiky Energy can stack.
source: Journey Together FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-03-27)

q: If I have Bravery Charm attached to an 80 HP Hoothoot with 120 damage on it, when I evolve into Noctowl does its "Jewel Seeker" Ability happen before Noctowl is KO'd?
a: The KO takes effect before Jewel Seeker could be activated.

q: If a basic Dragon type Pokemon has Protective Goggles equipped, would it take precedence over the opponent's Lillie's Clefairy ex's "Fairy Zone" Ability?
a: Protective Goggles will keep the Pokemon from having a Weakness.

q: If I use Klefki's "Joust" attack against a Pokemon with Handheld Fan attached, does the Handheld Fan get discarded before it can move an Energy from the Attacking Pokemon or not?
a: Since the Handheld Fan gets discarded before damage is done, it cannot move an Energy from the Attacking Pokemon to one of the opponent's Benched Pokemon.

q: If N's Darmanitan has Boomerang Energy attached and uses its "Flamebody Cannon" attack against a Pokemon with Handheld Fan attached, what happens with the Boomerang Energy?
a: The step to process effects such as Handheld Fan comes after the effects of attacks, so Boomerang Energy would be attached again when that check occurs.

q: If I used Alakazam ex's "Dimensional Hand" attack from the bench on the opponent's Defending Pokemon with Handheld Fan attached, would one of Alakazam ex's Energy cards be moved or not?
a: Even though Alakazam ex is on the Bench it is still considered "the Attacking Pokemon". So the opponent's Handheld Fan would move an Energy Card from Alakazam ex to one of your other Benched Pokemon if you are able to do so.

q: How do you Retreat using Energy Cards that provide more than one Energy?
a: Essentially you can discard a number of Energy cards equal to the total Retreat Cost, or you can discard until you've fulfilled the Energy requirement in the Retreat Cost; but you cannot discard more Energy cards than the total Retreat Cost. For example, if a Pokemon has a Retreat Cost of 2 you could discard either 1 or 2 Double Turbo Energy to retreat it.

q: If I use Professor Turo's Scenario on a Pokemon while my opponent has a Milotic with "Mentally Calm" Ability in play. Do any energies or tools attached to my Pokemon get discarded or do they stay attached?
a: Professor Turo's Scenario is still considered as played and it would go into your discard pile, but since your Pokemon did not get put into your hand due to Mentally Calm all cards would stay attached to that Pokemon.

q: Can Slowking use its "Seek Inspiration" attack to copy Terrakion's "Cavern Tackle" on successive turns if it used "Seek Inspiration" on the turn before?
a: Yes, you can. Slowking did not use "Cavern Tackle" on its previous turn, it used "Seek Inspiration".

q: If Area Zero Underdepths is in play and my only Tera Pokemon gets KO'd while Active, do I reduce my bench size down to 5 Pokemon before or after promoting a new Pokemon into the Active Slot?
a: You discard down to 5 Benched Pokemon first, before promoting a new Active Pokemon in this scenario.

q: If Area Zero Underdepths is in play and I use Professor Turo's Scenario to pick up my only Tera Pokemon that is Active, do I reduce my bench size down to 5 Pokemon before or after promoting a new Pokemon into the Active Slot?
a: You discard down to 5 Benched Pokemon first, before promoting a new Active Pokemon in this scenario.

q: If I have Togekiss with the "Precious Gift" Ability in play and I play Amarys, do I get to choose the order in which I resolve their effects at the end of the turn?
a: Both of these effects happen at the end of the turn, so the player can choose the order.

q: In a Prerelease tournament, can I use Ethan's Quilava's "Bonded by the Journey" Ability if there are already 4 Ethan's Adventure in my discard pile?
a: Yes, since the Prerelease is run as a Limited Format tournament, you can have more than 4 of a card in your deck!
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Surfer to switch in Yanmega ex, do I draw cards for Surfer first or do I use Yanmega ex's "Buzzing Boost" Ability to search my deck for {G} Energy cards first?
a: You must complete the use of Surfer first and draw cards, then you get to use Buzzing Boost afterward.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29); TPCi Rules Team (2026-04-16)

q: Can I use Team Rocket's Ampharos' "Darkest Impulse" Ability to put 4 damage counters on both of my opponent's evolving Pokemon if they evolve two Pokemon from their hand during the same turn?
a: Yes, you can. The phrase "doesn't stack" means that if you had two Team Rocket's Ampharos in play, you would not be able to use both Darkest Impulse Abilities to put 8 damage counters on each of those evolving Pokemon.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I have Team Rocket's Ampharos with the "Darkest Impulse" Ability in play and my opponent's Team Rocket's Zubat with 40 damage evolves into Team Rocket's Golbat, do I get to use Team Rocket's Golbat's "Sneaky Bite" Ability before it gets KO'd?
a: Yes, you can. Since both Abilities are happening at the same time, the owner of Team Rocket's Golbat gets to choose the order they are applied.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: Can I play an Arven's Greedent from my hand if my opponent has a Team Rocket's Arbok with the "Potent Glare" Ability as their Active Pokemon, if the Team Rocket's Watchtower stadium is also in play?
a: No, you cannot. Team Rocket's Watchtower only affects {C} Pokemon in play, so Arven's Greedent still has an Ability while in your hand and cannot be played due to Potent Glare.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I have two Rapidash with "Hurried Gait" Ability in play, may I use the ability once for each Rapidash?
a: Yes, you can.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: Can I use Team Rocket's Porygon-Z's "Reconstitute" Ability to discard two cards from my hand if I have no cards in my deck?
a: No, because the discard is a cost to use its Ability. If you aren't able to draw a card, then you can't just pay the cost of the Ability.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: What happens if I use my Team Rocket's Wobuffet's "Rocket Mirror" attack to move damage from my benched Team Rocket's Pokemon to my opponent's Team Rocket's Articuno with "Repelling Veil" Ability?
a: Your benched Team Rocket's Pokemon would remove its damage counters, but the opponent's Active Team Rocket's Articuno would not remove nor receive any. If you try to move damage *to* something that blocks effects, the damage disappears. If you try to move damage *from* something that blocks effects, the damage stays there.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Team Rocket's Orbeetle's "Rocket Brain" Ability to move damage counters from one of my Team Rocket's Pokemon do I have to move the damage to another Team Rocket's Pokemon.
a: No, while the damage must be moved from a Team Rocket's Pokemon the damage can be moved to any of your Pokemon.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: Can I use Team Rocket's Orbeetle's "Rocket Brain" Ability to move enough damage to KO one of my own Pokemon?
a: You can if you want to; there is no restriction blocking you from KO'ing one of your own Pokemon. However, you may not move more damage than required to KO the Pokemon because Rocket Brain only moves one damage counter at a time.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If my only Pokemon is Team Rocket's Koffing with "Smog Signals" Ability and it is KO'd by damage, do I get to search for 2 Koffing and put them on my Bench or do I lose the game?
a: Yes, you get to use the Ability before you lose. Team Rocket's Koffing takes the damage and you search your deck for 2 Pokemon with Koffing in their names and put them onto your Bench, then you check for KO's afterward.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If my opponent's Active Pokemon is Cetitan ex with the "Snow Camouflage" Ability, can I use Team Rocket's Giovanni to switch one of their benched Pokemon with it?
a: If your opponent's chosen Benched Pokemon is Cetitan ex, then Team Rocket's Giovanni's effect will be blocked. But choosing a Benched Pokemon without "Snow Camouflage" will cause it to switch with the Active Cetitan ex because the Benched Pokemon is the target of Team Rocket's Giovanni. You will still switch your Team Rocket Pokemon either way.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Primeape's "Drag Off" attack and choose my opponent's benched Misty's Magikarp with "So Submerged" Ability, would it do 30 damage to their Active Pokemon?
a: No, damage is only done to the "new Active Pokemon". The damage doesn't happen because So Submerged prevents Drag Off from bringing Misty's Magikarp into the Active Spot.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Team Rocket's Moltres ex's "Evil Incineration" attack to discard my opponent's Active Pokemon, do I take any Prize cards for that?
a: No, you are discarding it, not knocking it out.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Team Rocket's Persian ex's "Haughty Order" attack, do I have to pay the Energy cost of the attack I chose?
a: No, you only have to pay the attack cost of Haughty Order.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Hydrapple's "Hydra Breath" attack but I don't have six Basic Grass Energy to discard from my hand, can I discard the energy cards I have even though the attack will do nothing?
a: No, if you can't discard the six required Energy you cannot discard any Energy cards.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Blaziken's "Inferno Kick Flurry" attack and my opponent has no benched Pokemon, do I still have to discard 2 Energy?
a: Yes, you do. The discard of the Energy is a separate effect and is not optional.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Arboliva ex's "Oil Salvo" attack and choose my opponent's active Shaymin with the "Flower Curtain" Ability first with enough damage to KO it, can I then choose benched non-Rule Box Pokemon and do damage to them?
a: No, you cannot. All damage is done before KO's happen, so the Shaymin is still there to protect Benched Pokemon that don't have a Rule Box.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Arboliva ex's "Oil Salvo" attack while Granite Cave is in play and choose three Steven's Pokemon twice, how do I apply the damage?
a: Oil Salvo is a single attack. The attack's damage is calculated after you finish making all choices, so all damage modifiers are applied to the total damage for each Pokemon. In this example, each of the chosen Pokemon receive 40 damage (20 times two) which is then reduced by 30 for each Steven's Pokémon due to Granite Cave, so each will ultimately take 10 damage.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Team Rocket's Blipbug's "Searching Eyes" attack to look at one of my opponent's face-down Prize cards does my opponent get to see it too?
a: Your opponent does not get to see the Prize card, and you must replace it in the same position in the Prize area that you took it from.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: Can I use Misty's Gyarados' "Splashing Panic" attack if I have less than 7 cards in my deck?
a: Yes, you would do as much as you can.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If my opponent's undamaged Zamazenta used its "Strong Bash" attack last turn and my attack this turn does 200 damage, do I place 13 or 20 damage counters on my attacking Pokemon?
a: You place 20 damage counters. Remember, damage done to a Pokemon can be more than its maximum HP.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I use Team Rocket Nidoking ex's "Tainted Horn" attack and the Defending Pokemon is already Burned, would I also put 8 damage counters for the Burned condition?
a: No, the text of Tainted Horn is only referring to the Poisoned condition.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: What happens if I play Team Rocket's Bother-Bot and my opponent has no cards in their hand or no face-down Prize cards?
a: You can always play this card unless the opponent has no face-down Prize cards AND has no cards in hand. If there's no face-down Prize card, or if there's no cards in the opponent's hand (only meeting 1 of the conditions), you cannot make a switch but you would get to look at a card.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I play Team Rocket's Giovanni, who chooses which Pokemon to switch for each player?
a: You make all of those choices.
source: Destined Rivals FAQ; TPCi Rules Team (2025-05-29)

q: If I have Okidogi with the "Adrena-Power" Ability as my Active Pokemon and it only has a Luminous Energy and a Basic Fighting Energy attached, can I use its "Good Punch" attack to do 170 damage and also get the extra +100 HP from "Adrena-Power"?
a: Yes, although Luminous Energy only provides one unit of energy, it is providing all energy types all the time.

q: If my Team Rocket's Weezing is damaged by an attack, do I have to use "Smog Signals" to search my deck even if I don't want to or if my Bench is full?
a: The use of the Ability is not optional, so if you have bench space available you must search your deck and shuffle it afterwards. Of course you can voluntarily fail the deck search, but you must search and shuffle your deck. If your bench is full, then you cannot search as there is no place to put a Weezing if you did get one.

q: If I use Team Rocket's Larvitar's "Mountain Munch" attack against my opponent's Team Rocket's Koffing with "Smog Signals" Ability, do they discard the top card of their deck for "Mountain Munch" first or do they get to search using "Smog Signals" first?
a: The step to check for effects that activate when a Pokemon is damaged by an attack occurs after the step to check for effects other than damage. So the attack effect of discarding their top card is done first, then the triggered effect of searching is done afterwards.

source: Jun 23, 2023 TPCi Announcements (date approximate), TPCi Rules Team (2025-06-05)
Jun 23, 2023 TPCi Announcements (date approximate), TPCi Rules Team (2025-06-05)
